title: (No AI) The loss of Situational Awareness
author: Elizabeth Lopatto
content:
![A brain surrounded by blue lines as though it’s connected to things ooooo](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/STKS522_AGI_B.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Neither artificial nor intelligent.

I am not by any means an expert at finance but I think I do now have some advice for people who are: Do not name your hedge fund anything that will be hilarious if it blows up. Don't use a name like "[Long-Term Capital Management,](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-Term_Capital_Management)" or "[Amaranth Advisors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amaranth_Advisors)" (named for the floral symbol for immortality). Certainly do not call yourself "Situational Awareness," which might as well just be "Hubris, Inc."

Anyway, Situational Awareness, the hedge fund started by a 24-year-old former OpenAI employee that focuses on artificial intelligence bets, has sold [most](https://www.reuters.com/technology/citadel-buys-most-situationals-stock-holdings-after-ai-share-rout-sources-say-2026-07-30/) or [all](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/30/ai-hedge-fund-situational-awareness-citadel), [depending](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-30/situational-awareness-assets-fall-to-10-billion-after-losses) on [who's](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/30/leopold-aschenbrenners-hedge-fund-is-facing-steep-ai-losses.html) [reporting](https://www.wsj.com/finance/citadel-buys-situational-awarenesss-stock-portfolio-after-big-losses-in-ai-5117159b?mod=hp_lead_pos3), of its entire public stock portfolio to [Ken Griffin](https://fortune.com/2026/03/31/ken-griffin-citadel-securities-hedge-fund-miami-wall-street-trump-republican-politics/?utm_source=sfmc&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=NL_fortune-features_2026-3-31_108268&utm_term=fortune-features&sfmc_id=14949166)'s Ci …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/973467/ai-bet-situational-awareness-oops-stonks)

title: (No AI) LinkedIn actually adds a ‘seems like AI slop’ button
author: Jay Peters
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/1785424232227.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

A lot of content on LinkedIn might seem like AI slop, and now, you'll be able to report those posts. As part of a series of updates to reduce the volume of AI slop on the platform, LinkedIn is introducing an actual button that lets you flag a post as something that "Seems like AI slop."

The new feature is part of a broader push to reduce the volume of apparent AI slop on the platform. AI detector Pangram [recently found](https://www.pangram.com/blog/ai-in-your-feed?ref=404media.co) that 41 percent of longform LinkedIn posts were flagged as being completely generated by AI, [as reported by _404Media_](https://www.404media.co/linkedin-and-x-are-flooded-with-ai-spam-browsing-data-suggests/).

"AI slop is a top priority for all of us," chief product officer Hari Srinivasan says [in a post](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hsrinivasan1_ai-slop-is-a-top-priority-for-all-of-us-activity-7488612009660346374-xZiY?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAAIV1iYBHi7OPybalzIKilWBO4bTY5vJb8c).
